title: StaticBody3D with WorldBoundaryShape3D: Debug visualization does not match actual collision behavior
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4] ### System information Godot v4.6.3.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6750 GRE 12GB (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21041.1000) - AMD Ryzen 5 7500F 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.71 GiB memory ### Issue description After setting the fourth parameter of WorldBoundaryShape3D, the shape is visually positioned at -10m in the editor. However, when running the game, the CharacterBody3D gets blocked by the WorldBoundaryShape3D at the 10m mark instead. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a `Node3D` as the root node of the scene. 2. Add a `StaticBody3D` under the root node, and add a `CollisionShape3D` as its child. Set the shape to `WorldBoundaryShape3D`, and set the plane parameters to X: 1, Y: 0, Z: 0, D: -10. 3. Add a `CharacterBody3D` under the root node. Under this `CharacterBody3D`, add a `MeshInstance3D`, a `CollisionShape3D`, a script that allows movement along the X-axis, a `Label3D` to display the current `position.x` value, and a `Camera3D`. 4. Add a `MeshInstance3D` under the root node using `icon.svg` as a reference object. 5. Observe in the editor that the `WorldBoundaryShape3D` is visually shifted to the left at the -10m position. 6. Run the scene and move the `CharacterBody3D`. Notice that it gets blocked on the right side at the 10m mark. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [StaticBody3D with WorldBoundaryShape3D.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28890702/StaticBody3D.with.WorldBoundaryShape3D.zip)
